nodes.name: National Coastal Mapping Program (NCMP), executed by JALBTCX
nodes.description: Repeated topo-bathymetric lidar, imagery, shoreline vectors, and DEMs about 500 m onshore and 1,000 m offshore on a roughly five-year national rotation. USACE calls it the only federal coastal mapping program producing regional engineering, environmental, and economic data along the U.S. coast.

funding.note: FY26 allocation is 27% of FY23. The $15M authorization is a ceiling and is never displayed as spending.

unique_capability: repeat topo-bathy across the land-water boundary

nodes.cadence: About five-year national rotation plus event-driven rapid response

nodes.name: 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) repeat lidar
nodes.description: National terrestrial lidar. Baseline 99% available or in progress by end of FY25; transitioning to a five-year CONUS refresh. A baseline DEM is an archive; repeat lidar is an observing system.
funders: state, local, tribal, and federal cost-share partners

funding.note: Coastal-specific share not separately appropriated. 28% reduction in federal acquisition investment FY24 to FY25.

nodes.name: USGS targeted coastal surveys and rapid storm response
nodes.description: Beach and dune topography, storm response, UAS, CoastCam, bathymetry; morphology and model validation. Embedded in CMHRP. The FY27 request would maintain rapid coastal-disaster response on only one of three coastlines.
operator: USGS CMHRP science centers (St. Petersburg, Woods Hole, Pacific)

nodes.name: USGS Coastal and Marine Hazards and Resources Program (CMHRP)
nodes.description: The human transformation layer for coastal change: data acquisition and processing, short- and long-term coastal change forecasting, data preservation, and decision-support delivery. Hosts Coastal Change Hazards, DSAS, and the USGS half of TWL-CC.

nodes.description: Converts historical shoreline positions (1800s to 2010s) into standardized change rates with uncertainties. DSAS 6.1 released February 2026; national compilation May 2026. The software and old shorelines survive a cut; the workforce that adds and checks new ones does not.
operator: USGS Woods Hole Coastal and Marine Science Center

nodes.name: NCEI Coastal Lidar Archive
nodes.description: Long-term federal preservation of coastal lidar, about 1996 to present, all coastal states. Not line-itemed; NCEI's whole FY25 request was $73.29M. October 2026 cloud migration is causing intermittent degraded order fulfillment (an operational event, not a threat).

dated_events.label: NCEI cloud migration; intermittent degraded order fulfillment

nodes.name: NOAA Digital Coast and Data Access Viewer
nodes.description: Standardizes and distributes lidar and decision-support products. NOAA reports 75% of surveyed users said their projects would not have been possible without it and estimates a return above 400%.
operator: NOAA NOS Office for Coastal Management

nodes.name: Beach and dune morphology (USGS)
nodes.description: The USGS dune and beach elevation product that TWL-CC needs to say whether water will reach the dune toe, crest, or overwash. Built from NCMP, 3DEP, and storm surveys.

nodes.name: National Data Buoy Center coastal weather buoys and C-MAN
nodes.description: More than 100 moored buoys and 40+ C-MAN stations; real-time wind, pressure, temperature, and wave height, period, direction, and spectra. About 240 NOAA stations plus partner data. Shared by coastal erosion, flooding, and HABs. FY27 request removes seven coastal weather buoys (104 to 97), four currently non-operational, with nearby stations or satellite observations as the stated mitigation.

funding_parent.name: NWS Observations PPA (Marine Observations)
funding_parent.note: FY27 proposes a $1.803M reduction to Marine Observations.

dated_events.label: FY27 request: remove 7 coastal weather buoys (104 to 97); end VOS collection (about 5,000 obs/day)

nodes.name: Satellite marine observations (altimetry, scatterometry)
nodes.description: Placeholder node for the satellite observations NOAA names as a partial substitute for removed buoys. Not researched in this round.

nodes.name: WAVEWATCH III and Nearshore Wave Prediction System
nodes.description: Global wave boundary conditions (WW3) feeding the nearshore wave model (NWPS/SWAN), triggered by forecast wind grids from coastal WFOs and using RTOFS currents. Upgraded 2024.

nodes.name: National Water Level Observation Network (NWLON)
nodes.description: 210 continuously operating water-level stations on U.S. coasts, territories, and the Great Lakes; some records to the 1850s. One gauge feeds three clocks: real-time flooding, high-tide flood climatology, and relative sea level. FY27 request supports NWLON at reduced capacity: 185 remaining stations, comprehensive annual maintenance including precise leveling at 110.

funding_parent.name: NOAA Navigation, Observations and Positioning
funding_parent.note: Parent activity also funds CORS, PORTS, charting, and hydrography. $140M is not the cost of NWLON. An earlier $25M to $35M estimate was withdrawn.

dated_events.label: FY27 request: NWLON at reduced capacity; 185 stations remain, full annual maintenance at 110

nodes.name: STOFS family (ESTOFS, STOFS-2D-Global, STOFS-3D-Atlantic, STOFS-3D-Pacific)
nodes.description: Operational surge and tide guidance. NOAA states STOFS output is not total-water-level guidance; official guidance stays with NWS forecasters. STOFS-3D-Pacific v3.1 operational August 17, 2026, with river, rain, ocean, tide, and surge inputs: the first compound-flood branch.

dated_events.label: STOFS-3D-Pacific v3.1 operational

nodes.name: P-Surge tropical cyclone surge probabilities
nodes.description: Probabilistic storm surge guidance during tropical cyclones. v3.2 effective June 2, 2026, patched July 2026. Credited with zero U.S. surge deaths in the 2017 hurricane season (KCF brief).

dated_events.label: P-Surge v3.2 effective

sources.cite: NWS MDL storm surge technical notices

nodes.name: Total Water Level and Coastal Change (TWL-CC) forecast
nodes.description: USGS beach morphology plus NOAA waves, tides, and surge plus runup physics, giving hourly, six-day forecasts of erosion, overwash, and inundation potential. The operational convergence point for the erosion system; delivered into NWS AWIPS and to FEMA and USACE during storms.

funding.note: USGS portion inside CMHRP; NOAA inputs inside NWS/NCEP.

labels: No integrated answer for new storms

users: NWS Weather Forecast Offices via AWIPS

nodes.name: NWS Coastal Flood Watch, Warning, Advisory
nodes.description: Official coastal flood products from 122 WFOs, translating predicted water level into feet of inundation above ground, flooded roads, and property. Up to 40% vacancy at some offices (KCF brief).

nodes.name: Coastal Inundation Dashboard

nodes.name: PORTS real-time port systems
nodes.description: Water levels, currents, and met at about 40 ports, cost-shared with local partners. FY27 request retains the program. NOAA cites a 33% reduction in maritime accidents and 59% reduction in groundings since inception (candidate for avoided_loss after audit).

nodes.name: NGS Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS)
nodes.description: About 2,800 GNSS reference stations; vertical land motion that turns a tide gauge reading into relative sea level. Shared with coastal erosion.

dated_events.label: FY27: about 2,800 CORS retained

nodes.name: VDatum and the National Spatial Reference System
nodes.description: Puts ocean (tidal datums), land (NAVD88), and GNSS (ellipsoidal) heights in one vertical frame. Without it, a good water measurement and a good land measurement still don't give flood depth. FY27 proposes enhanced VDatum coverage.

nodes.name: High Tide Flooding Outlook
nodes.description: Annual and monthly flood-frequency outlook from NWLON threshold exceedances. 2026 to 27 outlook: national median 7 to 12 high-tide flood days, a record.

nodes.name: Relative Sea Level Trends and Extremes
nodes.description: Trends at 142 long-term U.S. stations with at least 30 years of record. Precision depends on record length: about ±1.5 mm/yr at 30 years, ±0.5 mm/yr at 60 years. Incorporates vertical land motion. Jointly supported with NOAA OAR Climate Observation Division.
